messages:
trina: Spotted a docs/runtime mismatch for /v1/files/upload. Docs show a multipart/form-data curl example, but the actual endpoint expects a raw binary PUT with Content-Type: application/octet-stream and chunked semantics. SDK snippets are misleading.
sam: Oh wow, that will confuse integrators. Do you have the exact curl you used against staging?
trina: Yep. Staging returns 415 when using multipart. Example: 
```bash
curl -X PUT https://api.redwood.ai/v1/files/upload/abcd -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data' --data-binary @file.bin -i
HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"expected application/octet-stream for binary uploads","code":415}}
```
harry: The docs generator must have pulled an old quickstart that used the legacy multipart approach. We switched to chunked binary PUT last quarter for performance.
sam: Can you open a docs PR to: 1) replace the curl example with a chunked PUT example, 2) update Python/Node snippets to use streaming upload from disk, and 3) update the error example to the nested error object?
trina: Done: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5012 
- replaces multipart curl with:
```bash
curl -X PUT "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/files/upload/abcd" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  --data-binary @largefile.bin
```
- adds a Python example using `open('f','rb')` streaming and Node example using `fs.createReadStream()` piped to fetch
- updates error response example to `\{"error\":{\"message\":...,\"code\":415}}`
docs-bot: PR created by trina: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5012
trina: Two follow-ups: 1) add a short note under "Request formats" explaining when to use chunked PUT vs multipart (multipart still supported by the legacy ingest pipeline but routed differently), 2) update the SDK snippet generator template so new snippets won't revert to multipart.
harry: I'll add the note and change the snippet template in the PR. Also adding a linter check that examples' Content-Type matches the runtime schema.
sam: After merge we should regen the SDK examples and trigger a docs preview. I'll take Node SDK regen, Trina can do Python.
docs-bot: CI: docs-linter failed initially (found multipart example elsewhere). Commit pushed fixing remaining occurrences.
docs-bot: CI: docs-linter passed for PR #5012  https://ci.redwood.ai/13421
harry: Merged and deployed preview: https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood.ai/files/upload now shows binary PUT examples and streaming SDK snippets.
trina: Verified Python and Node snippets locally against staging; upload works and error handling reads `resp[\"error\"][\"message\"]`. Closing out unless anyone spots more legacy multipart samples.
